Program ini mengkombinasikan pembelajaran melalui pengalaman, pembelajaran di kelas, dan pembelajaran melalui orang lain. Coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and production rollout activities. Support go-to-market strategies, product training, and stakeholder communication.

At Aleph, we design human experiences by asking the right questions. Here, you’d find a curious breed of creative engineers spread across the globe, specializing in craft, strategy, and technology. With a keen ear to the ground, we turn big dreams into user-first digital solutions by design. Through rigorous prototyping, close collaboration, and responsive engineering, we commit to creating a future that leaves our craft, community, and clients better than before. ​​We’re looking for a skilled and curious Product & UX Researcher to join our team and support the revamp of a major banking platform. You’ll be embedded in a cross-functional project squad alongside UI/UX Designers and the client’s Product and Business teams. Your role is to uncover user needs, pain points, and opportunities — and to champion those insights to shape the next generation of banking experiences. As the team’s Researcher, you will own the end-to-end research process and help guide both product and design decisions. You’ll also contribute to defining post-launch success metrics to ensure the solutions we create have measurable impact. Here are your key responsibilities: Collaborate with the internal project squad and the client’s stakeholders to define research goals and select the most effective approaches (interviews, FGDs, participatory design, usability testing, surveys, A/B testing, data analysis, etc). Translate business questions into focused research plans and activities that generate actionable insights. Lead end-to-end research: plan, recruit, conduct, analyze, and report — including managing research operations for the project. Present findings in clear, structured, and compelling formats (e.g., report documents, insight decks, or synthesis frameworks). Act as a user advocate in design discussions, participating in ideation and helping shape the UX. Co-define product success metrics and performance indicators with the team; help build a framework for ongoing tracking and optimization. Ensure all research activities adhere to ethical and legal standards, especially around handling sensitive customer and financial data.

As a Multimedia Designer at Odoo Indonesia, you will produce high-quality videos, graphics, motion, animation and other visual content that align with our brand . You will be involved in the full creative process from ideation and conceptualization to production and delivery—creating content that enhances our product marketing efforts across various channels. Additionally, you will collaborate with different departments and contribute to other creative projects, such as photo retouching and graphic design, helping to bring Odoo's visual identity to life. Your main focus will be on video production and editing, but you will also have the chance to work on multimedia design projects to create a broad range of digital content . Your tasks include but are not limited to: Lead the post-production process for product-focused video content, including video editing, motion graphics, visual effects, color correction, sound editing, and final delivery across different formats and platforms. Create engaging motion graphics and visual elements that enhance storytelling, product demonstrations, and marketing communication while maintaining consistency with Odoo's brand identity. Manage and contribute to the overall video production cycle, from pre-production and studio setup to filming and post-production, with a stronger focus on editing and motion design. Work closely with the marketing team and other departments to plan and execute video projects, ensuring the creative direction, visual execution, and final output align with Odoo's branding and messaging. Develop a deep understanding of Odoo's products to translate complex product features and benefits into clear, engaging, and visually compelling video content. Provide creative input and proactively suggest improvements to storytelling, editing, motion design, pacing, and overall video quality. Support onsite customer testimonial filming, studio shoots, and live streaming for webinars and other events, contributing to the production process as needed. Additional Multimedia Design Tasks: Maintain an organized archive of all video footage for future edits and reuse. Stay updated on the latest trends in video production and editing to bring fresh ideas and techniques into your work. Perform in-house photo retouching for presentations, events, and marketing materials. Workload Breakdown: Video & Motion Graphics: 60% of your workload will focus on video editing, motion graphics, post-production, and creating engaging visual content for product marketing, customer testimonials, webinars, and other marketing initiatives. Filming & Production: 30% of your workload will involve supporting and participating in the video production process, including studio setup, filming, lighting, basic production coordination, customer testimonials, webinars, and other onsite shoots. Traditional Graphic Design: 10% of your workload will involve creating static visual assets, photo retouching, and supporting other graphic design needs across marketing initiatives.

Position Overview Howel is looking for  Full-Time Merchandiser Staff to manage the flow of our products end to end, from purchase orders and supplier deliveries to stock, marketplace listings, and product development. This role goes beyond data entry. We are looking for someone who keeps product data accurate, follows up on every open item, and notices when quantities, prices, or stock do not add up before they become a problem. You will work closely with the Merchandising team and with other team to keep products available, correctly listed, and ready for launch on time. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys structured, recurring work with clear ownership and wants to understand how a consumer brand manages its products from supplier to customer. What Will You Do Purchase Orders & Deliveries Process and verify purchase orders (PO) and delivery orders (DO): create and send POs to suppliers, input incoming DOs, and check received quantities against delivery notes, coordinating with suppliers on any discrepancies. Follow up on supplier deliveries and shipment schedules, and monitor back orders (BO), outstanding POs, payments, and tax invoice updates in coordination with Finance. Stock & Marketplace Monitor stock levels in the system to flag low-stock, non-moving, or inactive products and errors in master product data, and take corrective action. Manage marketplace listings through the omnichannel platform (active/inactive status, photos, descriptions, quantities, categories) and maintain the weekly catalog, price updates, clearance, and bundle promotions. Product Development & Launches Support product development: keep the Trello board updated, follow up and review samples, provide feedback to suppliers, and join weekly Merchandising x Design meetings. Coordinate product launches: prepare launch briefs, request product descriptions and photos from the Content team, follow up designs with Creative, and ensure hangtags, accessories, and packaging are ready on time. Returns & Reporting Manage monthly returns: recap return data, coordinate with Ops and suppliers, and process return shipments and return POs. Prepare weekly meeting materials (PPT, repeat-order plan, returns recap, development updates, clearance proposals) and follow through on action items. Coordination & Periodic Reviews Handle daily coordination via internal and supplier group chats, and resolve cases raised by Finance, Ops, CS, and DC. Conduct periodic checks and reviews (showroom products, sample rack clearance, Google Drive files) and take part in seasonal development (Christmas, Ramadan), catalog and packaging reviews, and product quality tests such as towel tests.

About The Roles Make sure that every kilo a collector brings in is received, weighed, paid, and delivered onward — reliably, cheaply, and with data that holds up under audit. The Manager of Operations owns Wahu's physical capacity: how many collection points exist, whether they work, and how material moves from hub to MRF. Growth creates the demand; this role makes sure the network can absorb it. Job Descriptions Network build — hubs & dropboxes Owns the rollout plan against the 400–500 collection point target: site selection, partner onboarding, permits, installation, and launch readiness. Builds a repeatable installation process so opening a hub is a standard procedure, not a project. Manages the pipeline per partner and per region, phased against transport and MRF processing capacity  no hub opens that cannot be serviced. Proposes relocation or closure of underperforming points on cost and uptime evidence, with Growth consulted on whether demand can still be built. Delivers a hub that is ready to receive collectors on the agreed launch date, so Growth's pre-launch campaign lands on a working site. Hub operations — uptime and the collector experience on site Analyze and optimized hub for improvement Owns hub uptime: equipment working, scales calibrated, bins emptied, site clean and safe. Staffs and trains hub attendants; sets the service standard a collector meets at the counter. Owns payout execution  accurate weighing, correct rates (e.g. Rp 10,000/kg for aluminium cans), and payment into the app wallet without disputes. Runs preventive maintenance and a fast-response repair loop; a broken hub is a lost hub. Resolves partner-side issues at store level: space, access, signage, store staff cooperation. Logistics & collection Owns routing, collection frequency, fleet, and third-party transport so no hub overflows and no truck runs half empty. Plans capacity ahead of the rollout and ahead of campaign peaks flagged by Growth. Manages transport cost per kilo as a primary lever on unit economics. Owns chain-of-custody from hub to MRF — every load traceable to a source. Alignment with the MRF Coordinates with the MRF on delivery windows, intake planning, and volume forecasts. This is alignment between two organisations, not line management. Holds material quality at the handover: sorted, dry, and within agreed contamination limits  so volume is not lost at the gate. Gives the MRF a reliable forward forecast so processing capacity is planned ahead of the rollout, not after it. Flags early when network volume is about to outgrow available processing capacity. Resolves handover disputes on weight, quality, and documentation. Cost, data & compliance Owns all-in operational cost per kilo, hub to MRF  collection, transport, handling, payout  and drives it down as volume scales. Owns the operational data layer feeding the dashboard: volumes, weights, uptime, routes, deliveries. One source of truth, shared with Growth and Finance. Guards traceability so volume claims survive audit by partners, certifiers, and plastic-credit markets (PPRS, PCX Markets). Owns permits, KLHK and other regulatory reporting, and QHSE across all sites. Owns safety: this is a business with vehicles, machinery, and manual handling.

nama_pekerjaan: Registered Dietitian for Weight Management Program
deskripsi_pekerjaan: About the Program Our GLP-1 program supports patients on GLP-1 for weight management. Most GLP-1 patients in the Philippines are injecting with very little nutrition support — that gap is the job. You'll work alongside our prescribing physicians from first titration through maintenance. All consultations are online. What You'll Do Conduct nutrition assessments and build individualized care plans via teleconsultation; adjust at every dose escalation. Set and monitor protein targets to protect muscle and bone during rapid weight loss, and watch for micronutrient deficiency risk (vitamin D, calcium, B12, iron). Endorse supplementation or labs to the physician as indicated. Build plans around how Filipinos actually eat — rice as the dietary center, affordable local proteins (isda, manok, itlog, tokwa, monggo), merienda patterns, and handaan. Manage GI side effects — nausea, vomiting, constipation, LBM, reflux, early satiety — by adjusting meal timing, texture, volume, and fiber. Escalate red flags to the physician immediately. Prepare patients nutritionally for dose reductions and discontinuation driven by cost, supply, or HMO denial, well before they happen. Reinforce cold-chain storage (2–8°C) during brownouts and travel. Escalate immediately if a patient reports sourcing from unregistered sellers. Use motivational interviewing to build habits that hold post-medication; screen for disordered eating and refer out. Use the camera deliberately — ref and pantry walkthroughs, label reading, portions on the patient's own plates. Manage asynchronous follow-up between consults. Document in the EMR and practice per DOH telemedicine guidelines and the Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) — approved platforms only.
